subject.title: fix(agents): repair orphaned tool_use pairs on compaction prune path

question: Should compaction use the existing drop policy for aborted assistant tool-call turns, or should it synthesize a tool result instead?
rationale: Both options avoid provider rejection, but they expose different session-state semantics: dropping loses the interrupted turn, while synthesis preserves a fabricated result that may mislead the summarizer.

options.title: Accept drop policy
options.body: Merge this PR with the same aborted-turn drop policy already used by sibling replay sanitizers.

options.title: Require synthesized result
options.body: Ask the author to preserve aborted turns with an explicit synthetic result and add matching regressions for compaction planning and safeguard paths.

options.title: Pause for broader recovery design
options.body: Hold this PR if maintainers want a richer interrupted-turn recovery model before changing compaction behavior.

recommendation.title: Accept drop policy
recommendation.body: Merge this PR with the same aborted-turn drop policy already used by sibling replay sanitizers.

likelyOwner.reason: Josh Lehman is the listed compaction/context owner and is best positioned to choose the compaction recovery policy.
